column1: # UN/CEFACT Recommendation 20 units of measure - the curated subset PeakFlow invoices in.
# See database/iso/provenance.json. Rec 20 has over 1,500 codes; this is the subset that
# appears on invoices for services, software, utilities, logistics and ordinary goods.
# dimension exists so a comparison or conversion between incompatible units can be refused
# rather than producing a number. It is PeakFlow's classification, not part of Rec 20.
# decimals is how many places a quantity in this unit may carry - PF-247. Also
# PeakFlow's, and also not in Rec 20, which says what a code means and nothing
# It is per UNIT and not per dimension because the dimension is the wrong
# question: a minute and an hour are both time, and a quarter of an hour is an
# ordinary line on an invoice while half a minute is not a thing anybody bills.
# Counting units are 0 - there is no half of a pair, and a line that says 2.5
# NPR is a line somebody typed a gram quantity into.
# The column on a document carries six places, which is the headroom. This is
# what the unit ALLOWS, and the two are different questions: six places is what
# the database can hold, and 0 is what "each" means.
